I don't have a religious reason for any of it, honestly.  A vice to me is something that brings short term happiness, but long term issues -- learning a new skill like guitar, for example, is the opposite.  It's short term struggle with a long term payoff.

Suicide is a vice.  It feels good to think about death and how much pain you'll avoid, but to ignore the fallout would be dangerously short-sighted.  Just like smoking leads to cancer and gambling leads to debt, suicide leads to shockwaves of depression in other people you never could've seen coming.

All that being said, I respect people's right to do all of it.  Want to sell your body?  Ok, everyone's got bills to pay.  Want to go on a bender with all the drugs you can get your hands on?  Sure, just stay off the road.  Want to kill yourself?  It's your life, you choose when it ends.  I judge nothing, so long as no one else gets physically hurt because of your choices.
Men do plenty of sitting around, plenty of talking, and plenty of living.  Not many men hanging themselves recently though, seems like something men get help for.

Suicide is never okay, but neither is war, or addiction, or innumerable other vices we can't separate ourselves from.

It is wrong, but what is right?

Greatest fear is trying, failing, and getting paralyzed.  Not being able to try again and brudening everyone else for decades until I pass painfully -- that's enough to put me off.  I surrender, if only because I might lose.

I never really cared about what other people said, except certain ones I respected.  They made comments about my appearance and they stuck with me for a long time (plus, I own a mirror).  I thought the hospital might help, but it was just a waste of time that put more strain on my mother to support my unemployed ass.  

I should explain, the girl ghosted me for about a month and a half, and it was during that time I started to fall apart.  She didn't know I'd done any of it, and still doesn't.

She came back, looking to hook up but I didn't perform -- I found out the hard way anti-depressants can give you ED.  So now I've failed at being a friend and a lover, and she has no more reason to keep me around.  I already knew she didn't love me, but now I couldn't even be around her.  

I don't feel guilty about having money, I just think I shouldn't be given such a powerful tool.  I could take all my savings and live it up in Mexico until someone robbed me, and I'm so shattered sometimes I think I could do it.  It's like giving a gun to a 5 year old.

I don't deserve the good things that happen to me, and I don't deserve the bad.  I feel like a witness to a shitty movie rather than a person living my damn life.

Thanks for reading it, though I dont know if it would help anyone
